data.spiritual_symbolism: Meher: Radiant, Divine Light. A name derived from the Persian word 'Meher', meaning 'the compassionate one'. In Hinduism, it is believed that the goddess Meher represents the divine feminine and embodies infinite love, compassion, and mercy.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'māhār', meaning 'great'. The goddess Meher, also known as Mahishasuramardini, is a popular Hindu goddess who embodies strength and courage. She is depicted riding a lion and holding a trishula and a chakra. She is known to have slain the demon Mahishasura.

historical_references.reference: Meher Baba, a 20th century spiritual leader, was born as Merwan Rajaratman on February 21, 1894, in Poona, India. He adopted the name Meher Baba in 1922 and gained a large following through his teachings on self-realization and love for all beings.

Meher Mal, a Rajput warrior from the 14th century, is known for his bravery in various battles and for his patronage of the Hindu goddess Durga. He was a king of the Malwa region in India and ruled from 1336 to 1365.
